study_type.quote: The Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution TOPSIS method is employed to prioritize strategies using a balanced approach across economic, energy, and environmental indicators.

sector.quote: This study proposes a methodological framework to evaluate energy efficiency strategies in Colombia’s electricity generation sector.

region.quote: Colombia faces challenges such as the vulnerability of its energy security due to climatic events

method.value: Historical UPME/DANE indicators, LASSO regression BAU forecast (MAPE 1.2%), four PEN scenarios (Update, Modernization, Inflection, Disruption) with expansion and efficiency-upgrade models, AHP-weighted TOPSIS ranking of strategies by plant type
method.quote: Indicator weights were assigned using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) with expert input, and decision matrices were normalized using vector normalization.

outcomes.value: Disruption scenario reaches 95.3% efficiency in hydro and 61.7% in wind plants, 34% less fossil fuel use vs 2021 and carbon intensity 61.8 kgCO2eq/USD in 2030; wind strategies rank first in TOPSIS, then hydro; LASSO forecast MAPE 1.2%, R2 0.989.
outcomes.quote: The results show that the Disruption Scenario achieves up to 95.3% efficiency in hydroelectric plants and 61.7% in wind power plants, with a 34% reduction in fossil fuel use compared to 2021

technology.quote: Increases in the use of nonconventional renewable sources for electricity generation is challenging the system reliability, especially from the supplier’s perspective.

region.quote: using the Colombian electricity market as an application case

technology.quote: In this study, we assessed the coastal response to a WEC array on the La Guajira coast in the Colombian Caribbean using a two-step numerical strategy.

theme.quote: The installation of wave energy converter (WEC) arrays near the coast can have significant impacts on sediment dynamics and coastal morphodynamics.

outcomes.value: Containerized design with 60 PV panels (490 W), 6 inverters, 28 batteries and a diesel generator feeding 50 users; LCOE 1,274.76 COP/kWh in Choco vs 621.13 COP/kWh in La Guajira; PV supplies 1,206,950 kWh vs generator 114,872 kWh over 20 years in La Guajira.

theme.quote: It was demonstrated that taken into account the real options, the photovoltaic technologies are viable projects to be implemented in the commercial sector.

study_type.quote: it takes into account economic, environmental, technological and technical criteria, within the Colombian regulatory framework

sector.quote: Method (BM), to select the most adequate technologies for electricity self-generation in Shopping Centers (SCs); it takes into account economic, environmental, technological and technical criteria, within the Colombian regulatory framework.

region.value: Barranquilla (detailed case); Pasto and Cali compared
region.quote: The case study was based on real data for SCs in three different Colombian cities with different meteorological conditions.

method.value: Hybrid AHP-TOPSIS multicriteria ranking, then DCF with Monte Carlo simulation and binomial real options (surplus export, demand-response TOU) under Law 1715; 7 criteria weighted by 10 experts
method.quote: hybrid method composed by technics of Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS), the Theory Real Option Analysis (ROA), the Monte Carlo Simulation (MCS)

outcomes.value: Source availability weighted 40%; biomass discarded in all cities and wind in Pasto and Cali, so PV is viable everywhere and wind only in Barranquilla. Baseline DCF (750 PV panels, 4 turbines, WACC 11.5%, 10 y) was unfavourable; with real options extended NPV is positive: PV 273,758 USD (export) and 166,336 USD (demand response), wind export 130,676 USD.
outcomes.quote: When the RO are included, the extended NPV values (AVf) (see Table 8) acquire positive values, making the PV and W- ROe viable projects under the conditions evaluated here.
